# Cadair Idris walking routes

At 893 m (2,930 ft), Cader (or Cadair) Idris is one of the highest mountains in southern Eryri (Snowdonia). It’s a popular peak to conquer – here’s our guide to walking up Cader.

SaveShare

Legend has it that Cader is named after a giant called [Idris Gawr](https://eryri.gov.wales/discover/history-and-heritage/mythology-and-folklore/idris-gawr/). ‘Cadair Idris’ in English means ‘Chair of Idris’, while 'Cader' could also refer to an ancient fortress. It's locally known as Cader Idris rather than Cadair, but either may be used. The most well-known local fable is that if you spend the night on the mountain, you’ll end up mad or a poet. Staying overnight on the peak is definitely not a good idea, as the small shelter is exposed and could be dangerous in bad weather. There are many cliff edges to be aware of, especially in low visibility.

The eastern slopes are a regular haunt for fans of the Mach Loop low flying aircraft practice area, and on good days gliders from further up the coast swoop by high above the valleys below.

![A glider over lakes and an estuary.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2020-07/NVW-D24-2021-0154-small.jpg.webp?itok=gDs3gsB_)

View from the slopes of Cader Idris over Cregennan Lakes towards Abermaw, North Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

## Where is Cader Idris located?

For the people of southern [Eryri](https://www.visitwales.com/node/4041), Cader Idris is a constant presence in their lives. The distinctive shape of the mountain's peaks can be seen for miles around, from the coastlines at [Tywyn](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5455) and [Abermaw](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5547) (Barmouth) and high over the market town of [Dolgellau](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5887). The summit of Penygadair is a sharp contrast to the gentler hills below - when the clouds lift from the peak, that is!

The nearest main line railway stations are Machynlleth, Tywyn and Abermaw. Minffordd has a nearby bus stop, however you’ll need to walk a few miles from Dolgellau or Abergynolwyn to get to the other starting points. The [T2 Trawscymru service](https://traws.cymru/en/services/LLCO/T2) stops at Minffordd (bus stop name: Minffordd, Gwesty i Gader Idris/Hotel for Cader Idris) and Dolgellau. [Traveline Cymru](https://www.traveline.cymru/) is a useful journey planner for public transport in the region.

You can park your car at Dôl Idris (Minffordd), Llanfihangel y Pennant and Tŷ Nant. The Dôl Idris and Tŷ Nant car parks are run by Eryri National Park and there is a charge to use them - they accept card payments only. Find out the up to date information on the [Eryri National Park car parks page](https://snowdonia.gov.wales/visit/plan-your-visit/parking-in-snowdonia/). It’s best to get there early as they can fill up at busy times. The Llanfihangel y Pennant village car park is free to use but it’s very small.

There are toilets at each of the car parks which you should use before you start walking, as there aren’t any on the mountain.

![Two people looking over a lake towards the top of Cader Idris.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2020-03/NVW-C147-1819-0163-small.jpg.webp?itok=jsqf7fwX)

Llyn Cau looking towards Craig Cau and Penygadair, North Wales

## Cader Idris routes

### The Pony Path (Tŷ Nant)

10km / 6 miles, allow 5 hours there and back

The [Pony Path](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/pony-path-ty-nant/) starts from the Dolgellau side of Cader. It’s probably the most popular route, heading up the mountainside to the curve of the cliff edge above Llyn y Gader. Starting from Tŷ Nant car park (pay and display, toilets), it's a steepish climb with steps in several places to help you along. On the way you’ll see spectacular views over the Mawddach estuary towards Abermaw. Once you get to the ridge over Llyn y Gader you'll get fab views inland towards Y Bala and over the lake. Follow the steep path to Penygadair. Then it's a scramble up to the trig point.

![Rolling green mountains and sky.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__portrait__3__4_3_1x/public/media-library/2020-06/NVW-D24-2021-0127.jpg.webp?itok=KkHV9gYq)

### Minffordd Path

10km / 6 miles, allow 5/6 hours there and back.

The shortest route but the steepest. The [Minffordd Path](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/minffordd-path/) starts at Dôl Idris car park (pay and display, toilets). To begin, you’ll climb up lots and lots of steps, following a stream through shady ancient woodlands until you're above the tree line. You'll get a slight respite as the path flattens out a little bit before reaching Llyn Cae, then it's a steep hike up to the ridge above Llyn Cau and then on towards Penygadair. Your reward is wide ranging views down to Llyn Mwngil, towards Corris and Dinas Mawddwy and towards the coast. Take care coming back down from the summit, as it’s easy to miss the path and you probably don’t want to end up walking towards Dolgellau.

There are also [short walks](https://naturalresourceswales.gov.uk/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/cadair-idris-national-nature-reserve/?lang=en) around the nature reserve, including accessible broadwalks, to explore the lower lakes and waterfalls. Coed Cadair is one of Wales' [Celtic Rainforests](https://www.visitwales.com/node/6073), full of native trees and a wonderful, calming place to wander, surrounded by nature.

![A stone paved path up a mountainside.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__portrait__1_1x/public/media-library/2020-03/NVW-C147-1819-0057-small.jpg.webp?itok=5zSPA3B)

![A group of people sat looking at Llyn Cau from the Minffordd Path, Cader Idris, Snowdonia with Craig Cau (left) and Penygadair (right).](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__landscape__1_1x/public/media-library/2024-06/NVW-C147-1819-0176.jpg.webp?itok=69Dby1Zs)

The footpath and views of Llyn Cau along the Minffordd Path, Cader Idris, North Wales

### Llanfihangel y Pennant Path

16km / 10miles, allow 7 hours there and back

If you’re after peace and quiet, the longer [Llanfihangel-y-Pennant Path](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/llanfihangel-y-pennant/) is usually the perfect route to take. Llanfihangel y Pennant is a hamlet deep in the remote Dysynni Valley and an interesting place to visit in its own right. It’s reached by a narrow single track road, passing the romantic ruins of [Castell y Bere](https://www.visitwales.com/product/518051) on the way. The small, free car park and toilets are opposite St. Michael’s Church.

The path is fairly well marked. There are several places you can rest and appreciate the unfolding views of the Dysynni Valley down towards the coast or across to the summit. I do recommend you wear waterproof boots. The hillside paths can be very soggy, even in summer, and there is a wide-ish stream to ford along the way. Compared to the other paths, it’s fairly gentle until you join the Pony Path, then it’s a hard plod up to Penygadair.

Spend a little time exploring Llanfihangel y Pennant itself. As you walk out of the hamlet you’ll pass the remains of Mary Jones’ cottage. Mary was just 15 when in 1800, she walked 26 miles barefoot over the mountains to [Y Bala](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3258) to buy a Welsh language Bible she'd been saving up for years to pay for. Her story is told in the nearby [St Michael's Church](https://coflein.gov.uk/en/site/43893/), where there’s also an incredibly detailed, beautiful handmade 3D patchwork map of the valley.

You can find out more about Mary's story at [Canolfan Pererin Mary Jones Pilgrim Centre](https://www.maryjones.org.uk/) in Y Bala, and follow an approximation of her route along the [Mary Jones Walk](https://www.maryjones.org.uk/mary-jones-walk).

## Key information about visiting Cader Idris

**key-info** **Before travelling, check the** [**Eryri National Park website**](https://eryri.gov.wales/) **or their** [**Instagram @parc\_eryri**](https://www.instagram.com/parc_eryri/) **for the latest information on visiting, parking and conditions.**

There are three recommended routes to conquer Cader. It’s not an easy walk by any means, whichever route you take. They are all designated ‘hard/strenuous’ routes, and you should allow between five to six hours to get there and back. You’ll need to take plenty of food and drink as there isn’t a café (or toilet) on the summit.

Weekends and bank holidays usually get very busy on the mountain. If you'd prefer a quieter walk, head up on weekdays in spring or autumn. During cold weather the paths can be covered with snow and ice, so please don't attempt it unless you are experienced and properly equipped.

Cader is a very popular day out for school parties, sponsored walks, or group challenges, especially as it is one of the [Welsh Three Peaks](https://www.visitwales.com/node/2949).

![Sign pointing to Cader Idris in Snowdonia National Park.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/NVW-D24-2021-0165-small.jpg.webp?itok=yspjcVhE)

Tŷ Nant Car Park, near Dolgellau, North Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

### Safety advice

Fans of Susan Cooper’s _The Dark is Rising_ series of books will recognise Cader as the home of the disturbing, but thankfully mythical, _Brenin Llwyd_ \- the Grey King - who appears as menacing, thick dark clouds on the slopes above Llyn Mwngil (Talyllyn Lake). It’s hard not to imagine a malign presence when the clouds do come down when you’re half way up the mountain…

...so be prepared for drastic changes in the weather and make sure you check the forecast before you go via the Met Office [Cadair Idris forecast](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/forecast/gcm5z1ded#?date=2024-06-04).

- Plan your route carefully and let people know where you are going, and what time you expect to be back.
- There’s a full list of recommended kit on the [Eryri National Park website](https://eryri.gov.wales/visit/plan-your-visit/safety-advice/).
- [Adventure Smart UK](https://www.adventuresmart.uk/) has plenty of advice on how to ‘make a good day better’, and we recommend you read it before planning your day out.
- Please be respectful of our beautiful land and other people, and follow the [Countryside Code](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/the-countryside-codes/the-countryside-code-advice-for-countryside-visitors/?lang=en).
- Well-behaved dogs are welcome, but please keep them on leads as there is livestock on the mountain - follow the [Dog Walking Code](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/the-countryside-codes/the-dog-walking-code/?lang=en).
- Please take your litter home, and help to protect our fragile eco-system and wildlife by keeping to the designated paths for your own safety.
- Help Wales become the first Refill Nation by using nearby Refill Points to fill up your water bottle before you head off. Find out more including how to [download the free Refill app](https://smarturl.it/VisitWalesRefillApp) to find your nearest Refill Point on the [Refill Return website](https://www.refill.org.uk/).

## Frequently asked questions about walking up Cader Idris

- ### How long does it take to climb Cader Idris?











Depending on the path and your fitness level, allow between 5 – 8 hours to get to the top and walk back down.

- ### Which is the easiest route up Cader Idris?











The [Llanfihangel y Pennant](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/llanfihangel-y-pennant/) path is probably the easiest route for most of the way, although it’s the longest. The [Pony Path](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/pony-path-ty-nant/) isn’t too difficult, but all the paths have a scramble up to the summit.

- ### What is the most scenic route up Cader Idris?











All of the paths have magnificent views in each direction as you get higher - taking in the coast, mountain ranges and the rugged beauty of Cader itself. However, the [Minffordd Path](https://eryri.gov.wales/walk/minffordd-path/) takes you through ancient native woodlands, follows the curve of the cliffs above Llyn Cau, and provides tantalising views of the summit as you climb higher.

- ### Can children climb Cader Idris?











Cader Idris is suitable for some older children to walk up, depending on their fitness level.

- ### What is the myth of Cader Idris?











Some locals believe that if you spend the night on Cader Idris, you'll end up either a poet or go mad. Legend has it that the mountain is named after a giant called Idris (Idris Gawr). There is more information about this legend on the [Coflein website](https://coflein.gov.uk/en/site/406409/) and on the [Eryri National Park website](https://eryri.gov.wales/discover/history-and-heritage/mythology-and-folklore/idris-gawr/).

- ### What is the closest town to Cader Idris?











[Dolgellau](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5887) is the nearest town to Cader Idris.

- ### Can you see Yr Wyddfa from Cader Idris?











On a clear day, you can see the summit of Yr Wyddfa from Cader Idris.
